protocol.description:
This protocol is wlvision's private control surface. It is bound by the resident controller inside an isolated graphical session and by nothing else: the module that implements it checks peer credentials and refuses every other client.
Window handles are opaque session-local strings. They are never Wayland object IDs, are never reused after the window is gone, and mean nothing outside the session that produced them.
Revisions are monotonically increasing counters split into two 32-bit words, because the wire format has no 64-bit integer. Every request that acts on a window carries the revision the caller observed; the module rejects the request when the layout changed in the meantime instead of acting on a different window. Results and failures come back as events correlated by the caller's request ID.

interface.name: wlvision_control_v1
interface.description: Singleton manager global. Only the control user may bind it.

request.name: create_controller
request.description: Creates the controller object. A session has at most one; a second request is refused with a protocol error.

interface.name: wlvision_controller_v1
interface.description: Owns window handles, the revision counter and capture authorization for one session.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Reported in the error event of a failed request. The CLI maps these to its own error model, so their numbers are part of the contract.

entry.name: stale_revision
entry.summary: the layout changed since the caller looked

entry.name: window_not_found
entry.summary: no live window has that handle

entry.name: not_authorized
entry.summary: the request is not allowed for this session

entry.name: capture_unavailable
entry.summary: the compositor cannot capture right now

request.name: snapshot
request.description: Answers with a snapshot event followed by one toplevel_changed event per live window.

description.summary: move a window to a logical position

request.name: resize
request.description: Completes only after the application commits a buffer matching the configure sequence, or when the caller's timeout expires.

request.name: pointer_motion
request.description: Coordinates are logical pixels of the virtual output.

description.summary: press or release a pointer button

request.name: authorize_capture
request.description: Marks this session as authorized to use the compositor's capture protocol. The module keeps the authority decision; the controller never receives another client's credentials.

description.summary: first event of a snapshot answer

event.name: toplevel_changed
event.description: Emitted for every live window after a snapshot, and whenever a window is created, renamed, restacked, moved or resized.

event.name: frame
event.description: The frame sequence is monotonic for the session. The module assigns it at post-repaint and correlates the capture request that forced the repaint, which is what lets a caller tell a captured frame from a stale one.

description.summary: capture is authorized for this session
